properties.name: An identified issue is ROOT-CAUSED, PINNED BY A CI TEST, then FIXED — and the root cause is written down, not just the repair
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-08-26: *"if an issue is identified, determine root cause of issue, update CI tests to catch this, and then implement fix, and test… document the root cause of the issue as part of the design rule."*

═══ THE ORDER, AND THE ORDER IS THE RULE ═══

**① ROOT-CAUSE IT.** Not the symptom, not the instance. Ask what CLASS of thing this is and what let it happen.
**② PIN IT WITH A TEST THAT FAILS TODAY.** In CI, not locally. The test must fail against the unfixed code, or it is pinning nothing.
**③ FIX IT AT THE CAUSE.** `rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap` governs how.
**④ TEST IT.** The pin now passes, and the run is read from the authoritative object (`rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object`).
**⑤ WRITE THE ROOT CAUSE DOWN.** In the test's own comment and in the design — because the repair is recoverable from the diff and the CAUSE is not.

⚠️ **THE STEP MOST OFTEN SKIPPED IS ②, AND SKIPPING IT IS INVISIBLE.** A fix without a failing-first test looks identical to a fix with one: both end green. The difference only appears when the class recurs, and by then nobody remembers whether it was ever pinned.

═══ THE WORKED EXAMPLE THIS RULE WAS WRITTEN FROM (2026-08-26) ═══

**SYMPTOM**, reported from the field by hxm_program as F-01: replaying a gap into `gaps_to_prompts` exactly as the docs instruct — *"REPLAY EACH GAP OBJECT UNCHANGED"* — was refused with `invalid GapCandidate: missing field 'suggested_depth'`.

**FIRST-ORDER READING, AND IT WAS WRONG:** *"the budgeted reply withheld a field."* True as far as it goes, and it would have led to patching the budget to keep `suggested_depth`.

⭐ **ROOT CAUSE:** `GapCandidate` promises a replay contract IN ITS OWN DOC COMMENT — *"a compact row handed straight back to `gap_to_prompt` has to deserialize"* — and enforces it field by field. `description` and `evidence` carry `#[serde(default)]`; **`suggested_depth` and `affected_ids` do not.** So the contract held for the fields somebody remembered and broke for the ones nobody did. **The cause is not the budget and not that field — it is that a stated contract was maintained BY HAND, with nothing checking it.** Two mechanisms then cancelled on exactly the designs where both matter: the budget exists so the call can be made at all on a large design, and the handshake exists so the gaps can be asked.

**THE PIN:** `a_budgeted_row_replays_into_the_handshake_it_was_meant_for` — and it pins the ROUND TRIP, not the field. Serialize every budgeted row, deserialize it back, and separately deserialize a row whose optional fields are ABSENT rather than empty. **Any future field added without a default fails it.** Pinning `suggested_depth` alone would have fixed today and left the class open.

**THE FIX:** `#[serde(default)]` on `affected_ids`, `#[serde(default = "default_suggested_depth")]` on `suggested_depth`, defaulting to 2 — the value every detector but one emits, so a row that lost the field asks for the ordinary depth rather than an invented one.

═══ ⭐ ENFORCEMENT — SETTLED 2026-08-26: ADVISORY, NOT GATE-BLOCKING ═══

**Anthony's word, put to him with three options and a recommendation.** `enforced: false`. Breaking this rule does NOT stop the build.

**WHY, AND IT IS NOT LENIENCY.** The load-bearing half of this rule is step ②, and **nothing in a diff or a CI run can see whether a test was FAILING before the fix** — CI only ever runs the merged state. The note below predicted this before the question was asked, and the prediction held.

So an enforced version could only check something weaker — *does this change touch code and add no test?* — which passes on a test written AFTER the fix. That is the failure mode this project keeps finding and just spent a day fixing three times over: **a check that reads as enforcement while measuring something else is worse than no check**, because it converts an unanswered question into a false green.

⚠️ **THE COST, STATED RATHER THAN BURIED:** advisory rules get skipped, and this rule exists precisely because F-01's own fix skipped step ②. Its author verified the pin passing and never saw it fail. The discipline now rests on sessions choosing it, and on the record saying honestly which way it went — the fixes on 2026-08-26 each recorded that they WERE observed failing first, and that sentence is the only evidence there is.

📌 **WHAT WOULD MAKE PART OF THIS CHECKABLE**, kept because the answer may change: `req:a-rule-says-whether-it-can-be-checked-at-all` (ACCEPTED, unbuilt) is where the distinction between a rule's checkable and uncheckable halves belongs. And the ⑤ half IS checkable today — `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause` (ACCEPTED) asks a repair to record whether it reached the cause. Splitting enforcement across the two halves was offered as an option and NOT taken; if step ② keeps being skipped, that split is the next thing to try rather than gating the whole rule.
